data_unification.Diabetes: Healthcare-Diabetes.csv: Age -> age, Glucose -> glucose_mgdl (0 treated as missing sentinel; 18 zeros in raw, 8 remain after age filter)
data_unification.CKD: Chronic_Kidney_Disease/chronic_kidney_disease_full.arff: age -> age, bgr -> glucose_mgdl; '?' -> NaN; 25 @attribute names parsed from header; 3 rows with 26 fields repaired (trailing/embedded empty field) before parsing
data_unification.unit_assumption: all three glucose columns already mg/dL; no rescaling applied

methods.filters: age non-missing and 30 <= age <= 70 inclusive; glucose non-missing and != 0
methods.overall_test: scipy.stats.kruskal on the three independent groups (two-sided Kruskal-Wallis H)
methods.post_hoc: Dunn's test: ranks computed on POOLED sample with average ties; variance sigma^2 = N(N+1)/12 - sum(t^3-t)/(12(N-1)); z = (mean_rank_i - mean_rank_j)/sqrt(sigma^2*(1/n_i+1/n_j)); two-sided p = 2*norm.sf(|z|) (sf used to avoid underflow); Bonferroni correction p_adj = min(1, p*3)
methods.visualization: matplotlib Agg; overlaid density histograms bins=50, alpha=0.6, density=True; Diabetes red / Stroke blue / CKD green; KW H and p annotated on axes; figsize (15,9) dpi 100 -> 1500x900 px

key_conclusions: Kruskal-Wallis H = 628.13, p = 4.01e-137 < 0.05: blood glucose distributions differ significantly across the three cohorts.
Dunn + Bonferroni: Diabetes vs Stroke (z=23.37, p_adj=2.63e-120) and Stroke vs CKD (z=-12.77, p_adj=7.37e-37) are significant; Diabetes vs CKD is not (z=-0.44, p_adj=1.0).
Medians: Diabetes 125.0, CKD 123.0, Stroke 92.23 mg/dL — Diabetes and CKD are statistically indistinguishable from each other but both are markedly higher than Stroke.
CKD has the largest spread (std 80.6, range 70-490 mg/dL) driven by a small n (273).
caveats: Glucose is a single random/point measurement per record; no fasting-status harmonization across sources is possible.
Cohorts differ in age composition (mean age Diabetes 42.6 vs Stroke 49.7 vs CKD 52.9) even within the 30-70 window, and differ in disease context, so between-cohort differences are not causal.
CKD bgr has heavy missingness in the raw ARFF (44/400 missing), so the CKD group is a smaller and possibly selected subset.
Age-filter counts use inclusive bounds [30,70]; 3 malformed ARFF rows were repaired but all fall outside the analysis windows.
